questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was especially important that the university offered interesting courses. Furthermore, I wanted a university where the administration was helpful and the study program organized and structured. I also wanted the city to be interesting and beautiful.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had an amazing experience at Stockholm University. I met so many interesting people and learned a lot both personally and academically.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Stockholm University provided all the information through e-mail and was very helpful to answer additional questions. The university organized a zoom meeting before arrival where they talked about the university in general and important deadlines. Here you also had the opportunity to meet new people.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university had organized different events for new arrivals. At these meetups you receive important information about the semester. You will also meet your fellow colleges and just have a good time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the orientation and assistance available to students at Stockholm University. They answer e-mails very quickly and you feel that they take your questions seriously.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was not easy to find housing. The situation is quite combatable to the one in Copenhagen. I had no luck looking at housing portals etc., but was lucky enough to get an offer from a family friend. However, I had friends who got housing on their own by using housing portals, Facebook groups etc. So it is possible, I would just recommend to set some time aside for the process. I want to note that the accommodations through the university is not that nice. I had many friends who lived there and got more or less used to it, but it is not a very inspiring environment. The rooms are dark and the kitchens are dirty. Maybe you can be lucky with your flatmates regarding the kitchens, but generally it is not very clean.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Stockholm is an amazing city and there are so many nice areas to live in. When living off campus, maybe with swedish roommates, you get the opportunity to experience the Stockholm lifestyle in a unique way. I can highly reccoment it!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It is difficult to find accommodation, but it is not impossible. If you put in the effort you will find something. Maybe it is not the ideal location, but don't worry you will be out all the time anyways - meet up with friends, study at the library and just experience the city. 

I applied for accommodation through the university, but didn't get an offer. I am not sure how they choose who get an offer or not. It felt a bit random to be honest.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy to register for courses. It is very important to register at the exact time frame, to be sure to get your options. The institution will provide you with information about when and how to apply. I got both of my first options and my impression is that most others did too.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for the courses through an online platform. The link and the general information about the registration is provided by the university. It is very easy to understand how to apply.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A guide provided by e-mail on how to apply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got me first options.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the day and time for the registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had two very interesting courses: 1) Human Rights in a Global Perspective and 2) Equality Law. My teacher in 'Human Rights' where unfortunately sick a lot, which created some issues with cancelled teaching etc. It created a lot of confusion, especially in relation to our exams - we had to hand in both a case study, an essay, an oral presentation and a 4 hours written exam and by that time we hadn't had all our teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was an exchange student at my first semester of my masters.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of online classes as covid was still a factor. You need to have your camera on and participate. It is not like KU, where you can choose. All the classes are mandatory, which means that if you didn't participate you needed to write a make up assignment on what you had to learn that day. It is very motivating, but of course a big difference from KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Human Rights in a Global Perspective (15 ECTS) and Equality Law (15 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in Human Rights Law I would definitely recommend both the courses I participated in: Human Rights in a Global Perspective and Equality Law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: All the costs are very similar to the ones you are used to in Denmark. If you enjoy going out for dinner, partying etc. you will maybe find the drinks and alcohol in general a bit more expensive, especially in certain areas in the city. Generally, however, the costs are more or less comparable with the danish.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In some supermarkets the prices for certain groceries are quite expensive, such as meat.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is plenty of opportunity to take part in various activities organized by the University.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I participated in social activities such as meetups called 'Fika' and parties. I also played badminton at the university and many other athletic activities are available. If you want to learn Swedish the university arranges different courses.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Meet up with new people, ask your colleagues to go for a coffee, go out in the weekends, explore the beautiful nature in and surrounding Stockholm.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I spent most of my time in Stockholm. I enjoyed exporing the culture, going out for dinner, visiting different museums etc. I had friends who visited other citys such as Helsinki, Oslo etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - the Swedish culture is very much alike the danish.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: In the English courses you will mostly meet international students. However, it is possible to meet local students at the different social activities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are generally kind of reserved, just like in Denmark, but dont worry they will loosen up. Especially after a drink or two.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be openminded - all new exchange students are in the same position like you. Dont be shy, take initiative to do fun stuff. I promise you that no one will say no. Everyone wants to meet new people and have the best time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university in itself is really nothing special. The premises are old and not very impressive. However, I found the library and the student house good places to study. Don't waste your time in the classroom - go study elsewhere.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many amazing people - friends for life!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It gets cold and dark during winter. Make sure to bring warm clothing and to still go out and have fun even though it gets dark early. Many take D-vitamin during winter, especially people from the south.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You will not regret an exchange in Stockholm - just do it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
